messages:
incident-bot: Paging @mike-oncall for Seabreeze tenant in privnet - egress spike + failing client TLS handshakes seen from NLB targets. Severity: high. Links: https://monitoring/redwood/alert/ALRT-18055

mike-oncall: on it. digging into NLB health checks and target group. any customer-facing reports?

beth-customer-ops: Seabreeze reported increased 502s and timeouts for inference calls around 12:08 UTC. They see retries from their side. Impacting 2 production apps.

ryan-netops: I can see target connections dropping on the nlb-seabreeze-1 target group. Backend instances showing ESTABLISHED -> CLOSE_WAIT patterns. Possibly conntrack / sticky session mismatch after proxy roll.

anna-platform: Quick ask — is the tenant on dedicated pool or shared?

beth-customer-ops: Dedicated private VPC with single NLB in front of ded-gpu-pool-14.

mike-oncall: copying runbook: check NLB health, SG changes, conntrack saturation, and route53 weights. Starting with healthcheck logs.

jess-eng-sre: If conntrack is saturated, short-term mitigation is to switch NLB to non-proxy mode or shift traffic to ALB fallback. Can someone validate ALB health?

ryan-netops: ALB fallback exists: alb-seabreeze-fallback in same AZs. Health is yellow for two targets but PASS for app-level checks. I can flip Route53 weight to 30% ALB -> reduce pressure.

mike-oncall: Do it. I’ll also reduce NLB connection timeout and rotate keepalives on the pool. Runbook command to shift weight (route53):
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z12345 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"seabreeze-api.redwood.example","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"alb","Weight":30,"AliasTarget":{"HostedZoneId":"ZALB","DNSName":"alb-seabreeze-fallback-123.elb.amazonaws.com","EvaluateTargetHealth":true}}}]}}'
```

anna-platform: Patch applied?

ryan-netops: Applied. Waiting for DNS propagate (~TTL 60). I also opened ephemeral rule to allow healthchecks from ALB to backend SG to ensure pass.

jess-eng-sre: I’m running `ss -s` on the hosts — conntrack entries near limit on 2 hosts (95%). Flushing conntrack on those hosts temporarily. Command: `sudo conntrack -F` — doing one at a time.

mike-oncall: Flushed one host, traffic drop reduced. Customer 502 rate down 60% according to metrics. Good sign.

beth-customer-ops: Seabreeze confirms reduced errors, but still some timeouts on longer streaming calls.

jess-eng-sre: Streaming calls probably relying on sticky L4 session affinity. NLB -> ALB shift can break that. For longer-term: enable sticky sessions on ALB target group + enable prefix KV cache fallback to reduce long-lived connections.

anna-platform: I'll schedule a short maintenance window to reconfigure ALB target group stickiness and update the rollout policy to prefer ALB for 20% baseline. Doing now with minimal disruption.

ryan-netops: Also found a recent SG change request merged 15m before incident that added a restrictive egress rule on the pool management SG — rolling back that commit now.

mike-oncall: Rolling back SG change confirmed — backend connection stability returning. Monitoring latency and TLS handshake error rate.

incident-bot: Incident annotated as "customer-impacting - partial degradation". On-call: @mike-oncall. Runbook link: https://runbooks/redwood/vpc-egress-mitigation.

mike-oncall: Summary: immediate mitigations: conntrack flush, route53 weight shift to ALB (30%), SG rollback. Next actions: schedule durable ALB stickiness config, audit recent SG/iptables PRs, and follow up with Seabreeze CS in 30m.

beth-customer-ops: Noted. I'll let customer know we're stable and will follow up with post-incident notes. :thumbsup:

jess-eng-sre: Logging saved to /logs/incidents/1805554321/seabreeze_nlb_conntrack.log and snapshot of conntrack counts uploaded to S3.

mike-oncall: Closing the active paging. If we see >10% error re-rate in the next 15m I'll re-open. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
